{{Short description|Bolivian biologist and conservationist (1942–2019)}}
{{family name hatnote|Baudoin|Weeks|lang=Spanish}}

'''Mario Jorge Baudoin Weeks''' (September 4, 1942 – May 18, 2019) was a Bolivian biologist and conservationist known for his research in Bolivia and Costa Rica. He was the first director of Bolivia's national park system,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Steinberg|first=Paul F.|date=2003|title=Understanding Policy Change in Developing Countries: The Spheres of Influence Framework|url=https://muse.jhu.edu/article/41189|journal=Global Environmental Politics|volume=3|issue=1|pages=11–32|doi=10.1162/152638003763336365|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and served as director of several academic and government institutes, including the {{ill|Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de Bolivia|es}}, the Institute of Ecology at [[Higher University of San Andrés]], Dirección Nacional Conservación de Biodiversidad (DNCB) and the [[La Selva Biological Station]] in Costa Rica.<ref name="PIEB 5-22-2019">{{cite news |title=Profesor Mario Baudoin, una vida de aporte a la ciencia y al medio ambiente |url=https://www.pieb.com.bo/sipieb_nota.php?idn=11344 |work=Periódico Digital PIEB |date=21 May 2019 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mario Baudoin: un convencido de la protección a la biodiversidad |url=https://tipnisbolivia.org/2019/05/22/mario-baudoin-un-convencido-de-la-proteccion-a-la-biodiversidad/ |website=Archivo Documental Isiboro Sécure |language=es-ES |date=22 May 2019}}</ref> In the early 1990s he was involved in the creation of the {{ill|Servicio Nacional de Áreas Protegidas|es|Servicio Nacional de Áreas Protegidas (Bolivia)}} (SERNAP), which led to the 1995 establishment of [[Madidi National Park]].<ref name="PIEB 5-22-2019"/> He received the 2008 Distinguished Services Award from the [[Society for Conservation Biology]]. 

Born in [[Sucre]], Baudoin received his education in the United States, earning a B.Sc. at the [[City College of New York]] in 1967  followed by a master's (1969) and Ph.D. (1976) from the [[University of Michigan]]. He joined the faculty of the Higher University of San Andrés in 1985.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae: Mario Jorge Baudoin Weeks |url=http://www.beisa.dk/Participants/Mario%20Baudoin/MarioBaudoinPage.html |website=Biodiversity and Economically Important Species in the Tropical Andes |access-date=2 June 2019 |date=23 March 2003}}</ref>  From 1991 to 1995 he was National Director of Biodiversity Conservation,<ref name=":0" /> where  he secured several million dollars from the [[World Bank]] to support Bolivia's national park system.<ref name="Steinberg2001">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2MYkzBy2ka8C&pg=PA117|title=Environmental Leadership in Developing Countries: Transnational Relations and Biodiversity Policy in Costa Rica and Bolivia|last=Steinberg|first=Paul F.|publisher=MIT Press|year=2001|isbn=978-0-262-69266-3|pages=117–118}}</ref>  From 1998 to 2002 he served as General Director of Biodiversity under the Vice Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Forestry Development, serving several times as Acting Deputy Minister.<ref name=":0" /> Baudoin died in [[La Paz]] on May 18, 2019, at the age of 76.<ref name="PIEB 5-22-2019" /> He is commemorated in the scientific name of the [[bromeliad]] species ''Greigia marioi.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Will|first=Bettina|last2=Krömer|first2=Thorsten|last3=Kessler|first3=Michael|last4=Karger|first4=Dirk N.|last5=Luther|first5=Harry E.|date=2009|title=Three New Species and Two New Records of ''Greigia'' Regel (Bromeliaceae) from Bolivia|journal=Selbyana|volume=30|issue=1|pages=91–100|jstor=41760352}}</ref>
